title: How is an angle formed by turning one arm?
description: A compass is opened wider and wider by holding one leg still and turning the other leg about the joint. The same idea is checked on scissors and spectacles. Keeko's doubt, that the angle is the gap between the tips of the two arms, is broken by longer arms that turn the same way and leave a larger gap.
teaching_notes: One idea: an angle is formed when one arm is turned about the vertex with respect to the other, and the turn is its size. Watch for students who measure the angle by the gap between the arm tips.

source: Do you see how these angles are formed by turning one arm with respect to the other?
video_script.why: The child sees that every angle in the earlier examples is formed by holding one arm still and turning the other about the vertex.
video_script.substitution: Hold one leg of the compass still and turn the other leg about the joint.
video_script.anchor: a compass whose legs open wider and wider, with the same idea checked on scissors and spectacles
video_script.wrong_answer: the angle is the gap between the tips of the two arms
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the angle is the gap between the tips of the two arms. Longer arms turned the same way leave a larger gap, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: One arm stays, and the other arm turns about the vertex

final_answer.value: Yes. Each angle is formed when one arm is turned about the vertex with respect to the other
final_answer.spoken: yes. Each angle is formed when one arm is turned about the vertex with respect to the other

never_show: the statement that the other arm turns about the vertex, before the answer beat
maths_rules: An angle has two arms that start at one vertex, and its size is the amount of turn about the vertex.
In a compass one leg is held still and the other leg is turned about the joint, so an angle opens up.
The same holds for scissors and spectacles: one part is held still and the other is turned about the hinge.
So each angle is formed when one arm is turned about the vertex with respect to the other.
Slip: the gap between the tips depends on the arm length, so it is not the angle.
video_script.design: One idea: hold one arm still and turn the other about the vertex. The compass stays on the board and opens wider and wider. The wrong idea is that the angle is the gap between the tips.
